newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Engen says still wants Sasol deal.
newsitem.headline: Engen says still wants Sasol deal.

text.p: South African oil and fuels firm Engen Ltd said on Monday that it still wanted to try and tie-up with rival Sasol Ltd.

The two firms were talking earlier this year, but any deal was put off because of Sasol's uneasy relationship with the rest of the industry. Sasol receives state support which the oil industry says gives it an unfair advantage.

"The talks that we have had previously are being constrained at the moment, but there is no doubt that that they will come back on the table at some time and we will do something if it makes sense to our shareholders," chief executive Rob Angel told a news conference.
The oil refining industry is in the throws of a major restructuring.
British Petroleum plc and Mobil have merged their European refining operations and Shell, Texaco and Star have also come together in refining.
Angel said Engen aimed to prosper in this tough world of cost-cutting and mergers which was likely only to get tougher.
"We know that further rationalisation is going to come to us. We welcome it and we are going to be a key player in it," he said.
